paras: The West Carroll Parish lynchings of August 1890 were the reported killings by lynching of two Black men and one white man in West Carroll Parish, Louisiana, on a Monday night in mid-August 1890. Each man was accused of a separate offense, and the only known account is a two-sentence item from the local Carroll Banner, reprinted in a Lake Charles paper.

According to the Carroll Banner, "two negroes and one white man were lynched in West Carroll" on "last Monday night." The paper gave a reason for each killing: the white man was said to have beaten his wife nearly to death, one of the Black men to have "outraged a little white girl," and the other to have beaten a peddler. None of the three men was named, and the item gave no town or locality within the parish.

The account does not describe who carried out the killings, how many took part, how the men were killed, or whether any of them had been arrested beforehand. Because the Banner's own issue date is not known, the Monday in question can be placed only on or before August 18, 1890, the last Monday before the Lake Charles reprint.
No report of an inquest, arrest or official response appears in the coverage.

The Lake Charles Commercial printed the Banner item on August 23, 1890, in its "State News" column, between notes on drought damage to crops and screw worms attacking livestock. The Banner stated the accusations as fact and closed with the remark "Such is life in the country," and the Lake Charles editor added no comment. No other white paper and no Black paper was found to have reported the killings in August or September 1890.

reader.title: West Carroll Parish lynchings of August 1890
bases: The only report says two Black men and one white man 'were lynched' in West Carroll, each over an alleged offense (A1).

The Carroll Banner, quoted in A1, says the three men 'were lynched' for alleged crimes, which reports illegal killings framed as punishment, but it describes no mob, its size or the method, so a group of three or more is not shown (A1).
One secondhand brief, a Lake Charles paper reprinting a Carroll Banner item, is the only report found; no other white or Black paper carried it in the search window (A1).

accounts.label: Carroll Banner (local paper), as reprinted
accounts.gist: Three men, two Black and one white, were lynched in West Carroll on a Monday night, each for a separate alleged offense against a white girl, a peddler, or a wife.

framing.detail: The Banner stated the accusations as facts and ended with the offhand remark 'Such is life in the country'; the Lake Charles Commercial reprinted it without comment between drought and screw-worm notes.

No town is named; 'West Carroll' is the parish. City should be blank.
Three unnamed men: two Black, one white.
Agree: reported as lynchings for alleged crimes, but no mob or group size is described.
